model.title: Improving Access to Workers’ Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act of 2025

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to Senate):

blocks.text: Improving Access to Workers' Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act of 2025
This bill expands the role of nurse practitioners and physician assistants in providing services to injured federal workers under the federal workers' compensation program.

Specifically, under the program, nurse practitioners and physician assistants acting within the scope of their practice may (1) prescribe or recommend treatment for injured federal workers; (2) certify the nature of an injury and probable extent of disability; (3) provide prescribed treatment for injured federal workers; and (4) participate, with a physician designated by the Department of Labor, in a mandatory workers' compensation examination of an injured worker. In general, only physicians may fulfill these roles under current law.

This bill lets nurse practitioners and physician assistants take on more of the work of caring for federal workers who are hurt on the job. Under the federal workers' compensation program, these providers, when working within their scope of practice, could prescribe or recommend treatment for injured workers. They could also certify what kind of injury someone has and how much it is likely to limit their ability to work.

Nurse practitioners and physician assistants would also be allowed to carry out prescribed treatment for injured workers. In addition, they could take part, together with a physician chosen by the Department of Labor, in a required workers' compensation exam of an injured worker.
Under current law, only physicians can perform these roles.
